interface.title: METASPEQ Haridra NIR — Haridra Dry Extract NIR Quality Analysis (Streamlit)
interface.field: Analytical chemistry / NIR chemometrics for herbal-product (Curcuma longa) quality control
interface.stage_of_work: Method development and screening: applying and checking a PLS calibration, and reviewing its validation, before routine QC use
interface.what_it_is_for: Predict starch adulteration (% w/w) in Haridra dry extract from a 256-point NIR absorbance spectrum, with a green/amber/red confidence zone, and inspect the cross-validated PLS model, its preprocessing and complexity choices, a separate curcuminoid linearity study, and the model card.

data.note: Bundled study data (43 samples × 16 replicate scans = 688 spectra, 1.0–30.1 % starch) and a curcuminoid linearity set (30 levels, 0.5–15 %) loaded at start. The upload path was also tested with the copied example files spectrum_15.25pct, spectrum_00.99pct and spectrum_30.07pct (all valid). It was also tested with batch_7_spectra.csv and TEMPLATE_blank_spectrum.csv, which are invalid on purpose. Both of these have a text header row, and both crash the app with an unhandled ValueError. model_card.json was downloaded and read.

tree.general: Screen a plant-extract sample for an adulterant with a validated spectroscopic model and decide how far to trust the number
tree.specific: Estimate % w/w starch in Haridra dry extract from an MQNIR-DR26A spectrum with a PLS model and confidence zone; review the model's validation, preprocessing and limits; and check the separate curcuminoid assay's linearity and working range

features.name: Single-spectrum prediction with confidence zone
features.general: Pick a stored measurement or upload one and get a model prediction with a traffic-light flag for whether it falls inside the calibrated range. When a known reference exists, the reference and the error are shown too.
features.specific: Predict tab: 'Use a study sample' (Sample S1–S43 + Replicate scan 1–16) or 'Upload a CSV' (256 values) → Predicted starch % w/w, gravimetric reference with delta, Confidence zone (GREEN and AMBER observed; RED not reached), expected uncertainty ±1 RMSECV, spectrum plot with the shaded model band. The zone follows the predicted value only, not the error.

Pick sample and replicate from searchable dropdowns, or upload a file
Read the predicted value and, for study samples, the reference and delta
Read the confidence zone and the uncertainty text
Check the spectrum against the shaded model band

features.name: Fixed-length signal file uploader
features.general: Load a one-row or one-column numeric file of a set length as the input signal, then replace or remove it. Malformed files are not refused gracefully.
features.specific: Absorbance CSV uploader (256 values). Valid example files are accepted, '+' replaces the file and ✕ removes it. The 'Upload a single-row or single-column CSV of 256 values' hint shows only when no file is loaded. Known defect: any file with a text header row crashes the app with an unhandled ValueError that replaces every tab until the file is removed with ✕. batch_7_spectra.csv gives 'could not convert string to float: label' and TEMPLATE_blank_spectrum.csv gives 'wavelength_nm'. The numeric wrong-length message was not reached.

Read the prediction, or the error traceback

screens_never_reached: Confidence zone: RED. Every prediction I triggered from bundled spectra and example uploads (−0.11 to 29.10 %, including at 1 and 3 LV and with snv+sg2) was GREEN or AMBER. Per the reviewer's code reading, RED needs a prediction below about −0.8 % or above about 31.9 %, and no available test file produced one.
Numeric wrong-length rejection ('Expected 256 absorbance values, received N'). Neither invalid test file reached it, because both have text header rows and crash first.
snv+sg (non-derivative smoothing) view on the Spectra tab — seen in the Preprocessing list but not chosen
not_done: Did not get a RED confidence zone (see above), so its message and behaviour are unverified.
Did not reach the numeric wrong-length rejection message. A headerless numeric CSV with a length other than 256 was not tried.
Did not upload spectrum_04.76, 09.09, 20.00 or 24.81 example files; three valid example files were enough to exercise the upload path.
Did not test the Plotly toolbar buttons (PNG download, pan, autoscale, fullscreen) beyond box-zoom and legend isolation.
(1) The Model Card always describes the pretrained snv/8-LV model, even when the sidebar is changed.
(2) With preprocessing 'none', the cross-validated RMSECV (1.57) and RPD (5.44) beat the default snv (1.79 / 4.78), yet the static caption still says to pick the 8-component elbow.
(3) The confidence zone is set from the predicted value only, so at 3 LV S43 shows GREEN despite a −4.89 % error.
(4) Right after a slider change, the RMSECV 'selected' marker briefly lagged the slider before settling: it showed 6 while the slider read 3 (screens/025.webp vs screens/026.webp).

(5) Any uploaded file with a text header row causes an unhandled ValueError traceback that blanks every tab until the file is removed. batch_7_spectra.csv gives 'could not convert string to float: label' and TEMPLATE_blank_spectrum.csv gives 'wavelength_nm'. The 256-values hint seen in screens/038.webp was only a transient render during the rerun.
